title: Sexy Back — three opening bass notes
method: Hardware-only spectral inspection of the three separated opening notes. Settled families near 19.2, 38.5, 154–157 and 311–314 Hz are consistent with played Eb2/MIDI39 given the published dual-tone tuning: upper supersaw OSC1 raw+36/WIDEoff maps to physical+12 with +13 cents; upper supersaw OSC2 WIDEon is -12 with -15 cents; lower triangle WIDEon is -24 with -26 cents; lower saw WIDEon is +24 with zero fine tuning. Both tone octaves are zero. Lower saw higher harmonics near 622, 934 and 1244 Hz independently support the pitch class/octave assignment. Supersaw detuning, strong initial pitch envelopes and overlapping oscillator harmonics prevent exact single-frequency attribution. Gates are estimated from isolated energy rises/falls, with onset allowance for the patch's pitch transients. No Septum audio or parameter fitting was used.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. All three notes and timings are reconstructed from the hardware audio.
Velocity 100 is a placeholder; both tones have amplifier velocity sensitivity +8. Original velocities, controllers, system transpose and exact recorded patch revision remain unknown.

Upper supersaws have detune controls 78 and 37, different fine tuning and strong negative pitch-envelope depths -35/-33; lower triangle pitch-envelope depth is -34. Early spectral peaks must not be interpreted as additional played notes.

Upper portamento is on with time 4 and SOLO+LEGATO mode; lower tone is polyphonic, has overdrive and LOW CUT, and both tones feed the enabled delay. This is not an isolated oscillator or dry filter measurement.
Onsets and releases are estimated to roughly 10 ms. The high-frequency energy onset can lag the low-frequency attack; published zero amplifier release does not remove recording/output-filter tails.

The 1.2-second excerpt includes the quiet tail after the third note and stops before the next event around 1.25 seconds. Final note-off is an observed energy boundary estimate, not an arbitrary crop release.

The unchanged preset has static LP24 cutoff111 in the upper tone and LP12 cutoff95 in the lower tone, both with resonance0, filter-envelope depth0, filter-velocity sensitivity0 and filter-LFO depths0. Its dual-tone, drive and effect complexity still limits attribution of a spectral mismatch to cutoff alone.
No software audio or DSP parameter search was used to select notes. Preserve the published Roland preset unchanged.
